questions.q: What does creating a MySQL user@host account with CREATE USER grant by itself?
options: Automatic membership in the DBA role
Nothing beyond the ability to authenticate — privileges must be granted separately
Full SELECT access to every database automatically
Read access to the database matching the username
questions.explain: Authentication and authorization are separate steps in MySQL; a new account can log in but can do nothing until GRANT is used.

questions.q: What does GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON shop.* TO 'app_svc'@'10.0.4.%'; scope the privilege to?
options: Every table within the shop database
Only one specific table named 'shop'
Every database on the server
Only specific columns of the shop database
questions.explain: The dbname.* syntax is a database-level grant, applying to every table inside that one database.

questions.q: What is column-level privilege scope used for, per this lesson's example?
options: Granting access to every table at once
Restricting access to an entire database
Column-level scope does not exist in MySQL
Letting an account like a support agent see specific columns (e.g. email) while other columns in the same table stay inaccessible
questions.explain: GRANT SELECT (col1, col2) ON table restricts the privilege to named columns only, useful when a table mixes sensitive and non-sensitive data.

questions.q: What does the GRANT OPTION privilege specifically allow?
options: The grantee can bypass host restrictions
The grantee gains automatic DROP privileges
The grantee can grant their own privileges to other accounts
The grantee's password never expires
questions.explain: GRANT OPTION lets an account extend its own access to others, which is why it should be handed out sparingly.

questions.q: What does SHOW GRANTS FOR 'app_svc'@'10.0.4.%'; return?
options: A log of every query the account has run
A list of every account on the server
The account's current privileges, expressed as the exact GRANT statements that would reproduce them
The account's password in plaintext
questions.explain: SHOW GRANTS is the standard way to audit exactly what an account currently has without reading raw system tables.
